---
title: "Performance"
---

Wall time per milestone, measured on the development machine unless stated
otherwise. Profile before optimising; this page records what was measured,
not what was guessed.

## Environment

```{python}
#| echo: false
import platform

import jax

import jaxdft  # noqa: F401  (enables x64)

print(f"Python  {platform.python_version()}")

```

## Milestone 1a: empty-lattice band structure

Wall time of `band_structure` on the fcc L–Γ–X–U|K–Γ path ($a$ = 10.26 Bohr),
dense `eigh`, all k-points in one jitted, vmapped call. "First call" includes
tracing and XLA compilation; "steady state" is the median of repeated calls
with the same shapes. Measured when this page is rendered.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import statistics
import time

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from jaxdft import (
    PlaneWaveBasis,
    band_structure,
    empty,
    fcc_lattice,
    kpath,
    special_points_fcc,
)

lattice = fcc_lattice(10.26, unit="Bohr")


def timed(fn):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = fn()
    out.eigenvalues.block_until_ready()
    return time.perf_counter() - t0


rows = []
for ecut, n_k in [(2.5, 50), (2.5, 200), (5.0, 200), (10.0, 50)]:
    path = kpath(
        lattice,
        special_points_fcc(),
        [["L", "G", "X", "U"], ["K", "G"]],
        n_points=n_k,
    )
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    basis = PlaneWaveBasis.build(lattice, path.kpoints, ecut)
    t_basis = time.perf_counter() - t0
    n_bands = int(basis.n_pw.min())
    run = lambda: band_structure(empty(lattice), basis, n_bands)
    first = timed(run)
    steady = statistics.median(timed(run) for _ in range(3))
    rows.append({
        "E_cut (Ha)": f"{ecut:g}",
        "k-points": n_k,
        "N_pad": basis.n_pad,
        "basis build (s)": f"{t_basis:.3f}",
        "first call (s)": f"{first:.2f}",
        "steady state (s)": f"{steady:.3f}",
        "per k-point (ms)": f"{1e3 * steady / n_k:.2f}",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

At the smallest sizes compilation dominates the first call. Beyond that, the
steady-state cost grows with $N_\text{pad}$ much faster than linearly, as the
cubic cost of dense `eigh` would predict. That is fine for validation;
production cutoffs will need the iterative solvers planned for later
milestones. Basis construction is a one-off host-side enumeration and is not
yet a concern.

## Milestone 1b: Cohen–Bergstresser silicon

The same path with the local pseudopotential added: Si at $a$ = 5.43 Å, `Kinetic`
plus the matrix-free `LocalPotential`, 10 bands, dense `eigh`. Times include the
host-side `bind` (validation and coupling-vector enumeration) on every call.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from jaxdft import Kinetic, LocalPotential, diamond
from jaxdft.pseudo.cohen_bergstresser import silicon

si = diamond(5.43, "Si", unit="Angstrom")
terms = (Kinetic(), LocalPotential({"Si": silicon()}))
rows = []
for ecut, n_k in [(6.0, 50), (6.0, 200), (10.0, 50)]:
    path = kpath(
        si.lattice,
        special_points_fcc(),
        [["L", "G", "X", "U"], ["K", "G"]],
        n_points=n_k,
    )
    basis = PlaneWaveBasis.build(si.lattice, path.kpoints, ecut)
    run = lambda: band_structure(si, basis, 10, terms=terms)
    first = timed(run)
    steady = statistics.median(timed(run) for _ in range(3))
    rows.append({
        "E_cut (Ha)": f"{ecut:g}",
        "k-points": n_k,
        "N_pad": basis.n_pad,
        "first call (s)": f"{first:.2f}",
        "steady state (s)": f"{steady:.3f}",
        "per k-point (ms)": f"{1e3 * steady / n_k:.2f}",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Where the time goes, for a single k-point at Γ (median of five calls, each
step jitted separately):

```{python}
#| echo: false
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

from jaxdft import apply_H, hamiltonian
from jaxdft.calculations.bands import bind_terms


def median_time(fn, *args, repeats=5):
    jax.block_until_ready(fn(*args))  # compile
    samples = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        jax.block_until_ready(fn(*args))
        samples.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
    return statistics.median(samples)


profile_rows = []
for label, these_terms in [
    ("Kinetic only (1a)", (Kinetic(),)),
    ("Kinetic + LocalPotential (1b)", terms),
]:
    b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(si.lattice, jnp.zeros((1, 3)), 10.0)
    bound = bind_terms(si, these_terms)
    n = b.n_pad
    build = jax.jit(
        lambda s, bk, t: apply_H(
            hamiltonian(s, bk, t), jnp.eye(n, dtype=jnp.complex128)
        )
    )
    apply_block = jax.jit(lambda s, bk, t, x: apply_H(hamiltonian(s, bk, t), x))
    H = build(si, b[0], bound)
    psi = jnp.ones((n, 10), dtype=jnp.complex128)
    t_build = median_time(build, si, b[0], bound)
    t_eigh = median_time(jax.jit(jnp.linalg.eigh), H)
    t_apply = median_time(apply_block, si, b[0], bound, psi)
    profile_rows.append({
        "terms": label,
        "N_pad": n,
        "dense build (ms)": f"{1e3 * t_build:.1f}",
        "eigh (ms)": f"{1e3 * t_eigh:.1f}",
        "apply to 10 bands (ms)": f"{1e3 * t_apply:.2f}",
    })
pd.DataFrame(profile_rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Dense diagonalisation dominates. With the potential, `eigh` works on a full
matrix rather than a diagonal one, which is why 1b is several times slower
than 1a at the same $N_\text{pad}$. Building the dense matrix from the
gather operator is a smaller cost. Applying the operator to a block of bands,
which is all an iterative solver needs, is cheaper still by orders of
magnitude. The matrix-free operator pays off once an iterative solver replaces
the dense one.

## Milestone 2a: SCF for H₂

One self-consistent LDA calculation for H₂ in a cubic box at Γ ($d$ = 1.45
Bohr), with Anderson mixing and LOBPCG, and one force evaluation, which is
`jax.grad` of `energy` with the SCF inside. The whole SCF is one jitted call.
"First call" includes compilation for that grid shape. "Steady state" is the
median of three repeats.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from jaxdft import SCFOptions, dimer_in_box, energy, lda_terms, scf
from jaxdft.pseudo.gth import hgh_lda

h2_terms = lda_terms({"H": hgh_lda("H")})


def wall(fn):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    jax.block_until_ready(fn())
    return time.perf_counter() - t0


scf_rows = []
for box, ecut in [(10.0, 10.0), (12.0, 20.0), (12.0, 40.0)]:
    h2 = dimer_in_box("H", 1.45, box)
    b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(h2.lattice, jnp.zeros((1, 3)), ecut)
    run_scf = lambda: scf(h2, b, h2_terms, SCFOptions()).total_energy
    force = jax.grad(lambda s: energy(s, b, h2_terms, SCFOptions()))
    run_force = lambda: force(h2).positions
    first = wall(run_scf)
    steady = statistics.median(wall(run_scf) for _ in range(3))
    first_force = wall(run_force)
    steady_force = statistics.median(wall(run_force) for _ in range(3))
    scf_rows.append({
        "L (Bohr)": f"{box:g}",
        "E_cut (Ha)": f"{ecut:g}",
        "plane waves": int(b.n_pw[0]),
        "grid": "×".join(map(str, b.fft_shape)),
        "SCF iterations": int(scf(h2, b, h2_terms, SCFOptions()).n_iter),
        "SCF first (s)": f"{first:.2f}",
        "SCF steady (s)": f"{steady:.2f}",
        "force first (s)": f"{first_force:.2f}",
        "force steady (s)": f"{steady_force:.2f}",
    })
pd.DataFrame(scf_rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

The SCF converges in the same number of Anderson steps at every size, so
the cost per step scales with the FFT grid. A force costs about as much as
one SCF plus a first-order pass over the energy terms, as expected when the
gradient stops at the converged orbitals. The
[validation document](../validation/02a_scf_h2.qmd) runs about a hundred of
these calculations, up to 100 Ha, and takes several minutes to render. It
is the slowest page of the site.

## Observability: cost of the SCF log

Every `scf` call records a per-iteration history, which adds one Kohn–Sham
energy evaluation per SCF step. When the `jaxdft` logger is enabled at INFO,
the SCF also makes a host callback per step to write the live iteration
line. The table compares steady-state `scf` wall time at the acceptance
size, with the logger silent and with it writing to an in-memory stream.
The history is recorded in both cases. Each time is the median of five
repeats after a warm-up call.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import io
import logging

import jaxdft

h2 = dimer_in_box("H", 1.45, 10.0)
b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(h2.lattice, jnp.zeros((1, 3)), 10.0)
run_scf = lambda: scf(h2, b, h2_terms, SCFOptions()).total_energy


def steady(n=5):
    wall(run_scf)
    return statistics.median(wall(run_scf) for _ in range(n))


quiet = steady()
handler = jaxdft.log_to_stream(io.StringIO())
try:
    logged = steady()
finally:
    logging.getLogger("jaxdft").removeHandler(handler)
    logging.getLogger("jaxdft").setLevel(logging.NOTSET)
pd.DataFrame([
    {"logger": "silent", "SCF steady (s)": f"{quiet:.3f}"},
    {"logger": "INFO, live lines", "SCF steady (s)": f"{logged:.3f}"},
]).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Both times include writing the setup block and the final energy, so the
difference is an upper bound on the cost of the live lines. At this size,
the two times differ by `{python} f"{100 * (logged / quiet - 1):+.0f}"` %.

## Milestone 2b: SCF for silicon

One self-consistent LDA calculation for diamond silicon ($a$ = 10.263 Bohr,
HGH with nonlocal projectors) at 12 Ha, on Γ-centred k-grids of increasing
size, and one force evaluation at the 2³ test size. "First call" includes
compilation. The k-points are one `vmap` batch, so ideally the time per
k-point and SCF step is constant.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from jaxdft import diamond, monkhorst_pack

si_terms = lda_terms({"Si": hgh_lda("Si")})
si = diamond(10.263, "Si", unit="Bohr")
si_rows = []
for n in (1, 2, 3, 4):
    k, w = monkhorst_pack((n, n, n))
    b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(si.lattice, k, 12.0, kweights=w)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    res = scf(si, b, si_terms, SCFOptions())
    first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    steady = wall(lambda: scf(si, b, si_terms, SCFOptions()).total_energy)
    si_rows.append({
        "k-grid": f"{n}³",
        "k-points": n**3,
        "plane waves (max)": int(b.n_pw.max()),
        "grid": "×".join(map(str, b.fft_shape)),
        "SCF iterations": int(res.n_iter),
        "SCF first (s)": f"{first:.2f}",
        "SCF steady (s)": f"{steady:.2f}",
        "ms per k-point and step": f"{1e3 * steady / n**3 / int(res.n_iter):.1f}",
    })
k2, w2 = monkhorst_pack((2, 2, 2))
b2 = PlaneWaveBasis.build(si.lattice, k2, 12.0, kweights=w2)
si_force = jax.grad(lambda s: energy(s, b2, si_terms, SCFOptions()))
si_force_first = wall(lambda: si_force(si).positions)
si_force_steady = wall(lambda: si_force(si).positions)
pd.DataFrame(si_rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

A force at the 2³ test size takes `{python} f"{si_force_first:.1f}"` s on the
first call and `{python} f"{si_force_steady:.1f}"` s after. The cost per
k-point and SCF step falls from Γ to a few k-points, as fixed costs spread,
and then grows again. At 15 Ha the 6³ grid took 152 s against 23 s for 4³,
6.7 times as long for 3.4 times as many k-points (measured once while sizing
the [validation document](../validation/02b_scf_silicon.qmd), not computed
here). The first guess was memory: the density and the local potential are
built for all k-points at once, through arrays of shape (k-points, grid
points, bands), about 0.3 GB on 6³. The cluster runs in the next section
point to the eigensolver instead.

## Milestone 2b on biocloud: cost against the k-grid

The same silicon calculation at 12 Ha on Γ-centred n³ grids up to 8³, run on
the biocloud Slurm cluster through shephex (one job per grid, 8 CPUs each).
The numbers are read from `reference/biocloud_si_kgrid/`, whose README
records how they were made; they are not recomputed at render time.
"eig it" is the sum over SCF steps of the largest number of LOBPCG iterations
over the k-points.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

import altair as alt

from jaxdft.plotting import style
from jaxdft.scf.scf import EIGEN_TOL_FRACTION

style.enable()

cluster = json.loads(
    Path("../../reference/biocloud_si_kgrid/si_kgrid_scaling.json").read_text()
)["experiments"]
cluster_rows = []
for e in cluster:
    n_k, eig_it = e["n_kpoints"], sum(e["eig_iterations_steady"])
    assert e["eig_iterations_first"] == e["eig_iterations_steady"]
    cluster_rows.append({
        "k-grid": f"{e['n']}³",
        "k-points": n_k,
        "node": e["node"],
        "SCF iterations": e["n_iter"],
        "eig it": eig_it,
        "SCF steady (s)": e["steady_s"],
        "ms per k-point and step": 1e3 * e["steady_s"] / n_k / e["n_iter"],
        "ms per k-point and eig it": 1e3 * e["steady_s"] / n_k / eig_it,
        "peak memory (GB)": e["peak_memory_gb"],
    })
cluster_df = pd.DataFrame(cluster_rows)
first, last = cluster_rows[0], cluster_rows[-1]
step_growth = last["ms per k-point and step"] / first["ms per k-point and step"]
eig_growth = last["eig it"] / first["eig it"]
per_it = cluster_df["ms per k-point and eig it"]
cluster_df.style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| column: page-inset
long = cluster_df.melt(
    id_vars=["k-points"],
    value_vars=["ms per k-point and step", "ms per k-point and eig it"],
    var_name="normalised by",
    value_name="ms",
)
alt.Chart(long).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X("k-points:Q", scale=alt.Scale(type="log"), title="k-points"),
    y=alt.Y("ms:Q", scale=alt.Scale(type="log"), title="steady wall time (ms)"),
    color=alt.Color("normalised by:N", legend=alt.Legend(orient="top")),
    tooltip=["k-points", "normalised by", alt.Tooltip("ms:Q", format=".2f")],
).properties(width=style.WIDTH, height=style.HEIGHT)
```

From 1 to `{python} last["k-points"]` k-points the cost per k-point and SCF
step grows `{python} f"{step_growth:.1f}"`-fold, and the number of eigensolver
iterations `{python} f"{eig_growth:.1f}"`-fold. Per eigensolver iteration the
cost per k-point stays between `{python} f"{per_it.min():.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{per_it.max():.1f}"` ms, with no trend in the batch size. The
k-points are one `vmap` batch, so LOBPCG iterates until the slowest k-point
has converged, and the more k-points, the slower the slowest. Every SCF step
asks for residuals of
`{python} f"{100 * EIGEN_TOL_FRACTION:g}"` % of the SCF tolerance, also while the density is
far from converged. Peak memory grows linearly, to
`{python} f"{last['peak memory (GB)']:.1f}"` GB at
`{python} last["k-points"]` k-points, and is not the bottleneck.

The jobs ran at the same time on three nodes, one measurement each; the step
in cost per iteration between 27 and 64 k-points coincides with a change of
node.
